Title: Three teenage girls involved in scuffle over photo
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Police are investigating a fight involving three teenage girls at Dataran Melang here that went viral on social media.
Kuala Pilah police chief Superintendent Muhamad Mustafah Hussin said police received a report over the incident last Wednesday.
He said the incident involved a 15-year-old female student who had gone to Dataran Melang with her brother to meet two acquaintances over a misunderstanding following the circulation of her photograph on social media.
"A scuffle broke out during the meeting between the complainant and the two girls, leaving her injured," he said in a statement today.
Mustafah said the teenager later returned home with her family before she and her father went to one of the girl's homes the following day to discuss the matter, after which a police report was lodged.
"Police take the incident seriously and are investigating to determine the actual cause of the fight and identify those involved," he said.
Those with information can contact the Kuala Pilah district police headquarters at 06-48429999, investigating officer Sergeant Shamsuldalila Mohamad at 011-10129038, or any nearby police station.

Title: #NSTviral: Tunku Azizah steals the show in surprise TikTok livestream appearance [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A TikTok livestream at a boutique in Bangsar took an unexpected turn when Tengku Ampuan Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, dropped by and joined the staff on camera.
The boutique shared the moment on Threads, describing the visit as one of its most memorable experiences as it happened while staff were livestreaming.
"Imagine you are in the middle of a livestream and suddenly Tunku Azizah walks in.
"That was an unforgettable moment for us yesterday when Tunku stopped by our boutique in Bangsar. Tunku even joined our TikTok livestream with our staff," it said.
During the visit, Tunku Azizah also selected a telekung as a gift.
The boutique expressed its appreciation for the royal's support and trust, describing the visit as a great honour.
Her spontaneous appearance and relaxed manner quickly drew attention on social media, with users praising her humility and down-to-earth personality.
"Reviewer from the highest level," joked Durrashahirah.
Another user, Marianiyoon, was charmed by the way Tunku Azizah referred to herself as "saya".
"Aww, Tunku Azizah is so adorable. She refers to herself as 'saya'. So humble. She even offered a prayer. I pray that Tunku will always be in good health too," she wrote.
Meanwhile, Zamri_mac_arm praised the royal's approachable nature.
"She seems to forget that she is royalty… she is truly very humble," the user commented.

Title: 'Subpoenaed to attend TH RCI, but told to go home' - Madinah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former auditor general Tan Sri Dr Madinah Mohamad has defended her attendance at the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), saying she was there after receiving a subpoena but was later told to go home without being called to give evidence.
"I attended the proceedings because I had received a subpoena, but was told to go home without being called to give evidence before the RCI on the date they had set," she said when contacted.
Madinah said claims made by
TH chairman Tan Sri Rashid Hussain
, who is also an RCI member, regarding her attendance at the proceedings were inaccurate.
She said she had never asked to enter the RCI hearing room with then National Audit Department Financial Audit Division deputy director Dr Mona Othman.
Instead, she said Mona was with her outside the hearing room at the time to "stand by" in case any additional technical information concerning TH was required.
"The statement is inaccurate because I never asked to attend the proceedings with Mona. She was only 'on standby' outside in case there were questions of a technical nature.
"I never asked to enter the hearing room with Mona. At the time, a member of the secretariat came out of the hearing room and informed me that I did not need to enter and asked me to go home.
"If it was true that Mona could not be brought in, why wasn't I informed and why was I the only one told to go home? When I asked why, the person said they were not sure," she said.
Madinah also confirmed that she had received a subpoena to give evidence before the RCI and attended the proceedings on June 3, 2022, on that basis.
On the opportunity given by the RCI for her to submit written answers to 75 questions, Madinah stressed that written responses could not replace oral testimony.
"I did submit an affidavit, but it cannot replace oral testimony. They need to hear what I have to say," she said.
Madinah was previously reported as saying that
the RM4.8 billion discrepancy
between the National Audit Department's findings and PricewaterhouseCoopers' (PwC) assessment of TH was not evidence of any failure by the department, but should be understood in the context of differences in mandates, scope, reference periods and valuation methods.
She said the findings did not mean the National Audit Department had overlooked losses or that PwC had overvalued them. Instead, different figures could arise when different valuation bases were used.
She said the National Audit Department conducted its audit based on its statutory mandate, as well as the laws and accounting standards in force when the financial statements were prepared.
"For this reason, it is not appropriate to immediately conclude that the discrepancy undermines the credibility of the National Audit Department or that all audits previously conducted by the department should be called into question.
"Audit work must be assessed based on the laws, mandate and standards in force at the time it was carried out. It is inappropriate to assess a previous audit using standards or approaches that emerged later," she said.

Title: Ringgit opens firmer against greenback after Bank Negara holds OPR
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened firmer against the US dollar on Friday, buoyed by improved sentiment after Bank Negara Malaysia kept its overnight policy rate (OPR) unchanged at 2.75 per cent.
At 8am, the local currency rose to 4.0370/0420 against the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0405/0445.
On Thursday, BNM's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) decided to maintain the OPR at 2.75 per cent.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the MPC's decision to keep the OPR steady amid robust growth and fairly benign inflation dynamics suggested that the Malaysian economy was in a "sweet spot".
"This should provide support to the ringgit as BNM has policy flexibility, which can be a selling point for holding more ringgit," he told Bernama.
Meanwhile, Mohd Afzanizam said the ringgit also benefited from a softer US dollar following US Federal Reserve (Fed) Governor Christopher Waller's remarks overnight, which reduced expectations of a rate hike at the Fed's September meeting.
He said Waller's comments indicated that he would support keeping interest rates unchanged if inflation continued to ease towards the Fed's two per cent target, putting further pressure on the greenback.
"This US dollar weakness is broadly supportive of emerging market currencies, including the ringgit," he said.
Against a basket of major currencies, the ringgit weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5936/5970 from 2.5838/5865 at Thursday's close, eased against the British pound to 5.4608/4676 from 5.4539/4593 and dipped against the euro to 4.6942/7000 from 4.6894/6940 previously.
The ringgit traded mostly lower against regional currencies.
It declined against the Singapore dollar to 3.1868/1910 from 3.1850/1884 and fell against the Thai baht to 12.2668/2898 from 12.2421/2598 at Thursday's close.
The ringgit was flat against the Philippine peso at 6.46/6.47 but gained against the Indonesian rupiah to 228.3/228.7 from 228.5/228.8 previously.

Title: 'Do not leave your fate in the hands of the elite' - Sanusi
Article:
KOTA BARU: The elite should no longer determine the country's direction, with ordinary Malaysians now needing to rise and have a greater say in shaping the nation's future, said Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor.
He said the elite made up only about 10 per cent of Malaysia's population but controlled a large share of the country's wealth.
"An estimated 75 to 80 per cent of the country's wealth is owned by this group, while 90 per cent of Malaysians share only about 25 per cent of the wealth.
"I think this is unfair. So, it is time for ordinary people to determine our own fate. Do not leave your fate in the hands of the elite. They do not understand us," he said during the Podcast Anak Muda held in conjunction with the 72nd Pas Muktamar.
Sanusi said the elite not only did not understand the everyday language used by ordinary people, let alone the realities and hardships they faced.
He said this had caused some among the elite to take offence when colloquial terms used by the masses were perceived as crude, or misinterpreted as disrespectful, gangster-like or abusive.
"They do not use such language and they do not mix with us enough to hear us when we say things like 'mampus cabut' (get lost). That is normal in everyday conversations among ordinary people.
"Likewise, 'biar mampus belah halilintar' (go to hell). They are used to living in comfort, so how would they understand all this?
"Therefore, it should be the ordinary people who determine the direction of this country because they are the majority and share only a small portion of the economy's wealth. The country's structure needs to change. We cannot let this continue," he said.
Sanusi said his remarks did not mean that all children of members of parliament failed to understand the struggles of ordinary people, but were directed at children of the elite who had grown up in wealth and privilege.
"Those who are born into abundance do not understand people who are struggling.
"They only pretend to understand, but they do not. So, I speak, lead and handle matters from the perspective of those who are struggling," he said.

Title: RNG Tech Thai unit lands exclusive Lotus's massage chair deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: RNG Tech Bhd's Thai unit has secured a three-and-a-half-year partnership with CP Axtra Public Company Ltd to exclusively provide and operate massage chairs at selected Lotus's stores across Thailand.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said Rest n Go (Thailand) Company Ltd entered into a memorandum of agreement with CP Axtra on Sept 2, covering Lotus's hypermarkets, supermarkets and community malls.
Under the agreement, Rest n Go Thailand will be the sole provider and operator of vending massage chair services at locations to be agreed by both parties.
The initial rollout targets between 1,400 and 1,600 massage chairs across an estimated 4,800 square metres of space within Lotus's stores.
The contract will run from Nov 1, 2026 to April 30, 2030, comprising an initial six-month temporary phase followed by a three-year permanent phase.
RNG Tech said the partnership was part of its strategy to expand its vending massage chair network in Thailand, which the group has identified as a key growth market following its earlier entry into Lotus's and Big C outlets.
"The partnership is expected to broaden Rest n Go's footprint in high-traffic retail locations in Thailand, and is consistent with the group's broader publicly stated Asean expansion plans," it said.
Rest n Go Thailand won a Lotus's tender in 2025 and currently operates 806 massage chairs across 132 Lotus's locations in the country.
RNG Tech said the partnership was also expected to strengthen Rest n Go Thailand's relationship with CP Axtra and support its strategy of securing exclusive placements with leading regional retail groups.
CP Axtra, which is listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand, was formed from the merger of Siam Makro and Lotus's and operates retail and wholesale formats across Thailand.
RNG Tech said the agreement is expected to contribute positively to the group's earnings over its duration.

Title: How Zetrix bet on its future and lost two-thirds of its value
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd's bet on its own shares seems to have been a bad call for the artificial intelligence and blockchain company after its share price slumped nearly 67 per cent in just four trading days.
The slump, equivalent to RM3.55 billion in market value being wiped out between Aug 27 and Sept 2, came after Zetrix had been buying back its shares on the open market between January and August.
Zetrix purchased about 123.29 million shares during the eight months — including 32.46 million in July and August alone — for a total cash outlay of about RM94.2 million.
While a share buyback can signal a company's confidence in its own prospects and may be intended to increase shareholder returns, the margin call and forced selling involving shares held by its managing director and single-largest shareholder Wong Thean Soon reversed that trajectory.
On Aug 28, just two days after Zetrix made its last share buyback of 933,300 shares at 66.5 sen apiece, Wong disposed of 99.8 million shares at 29.9 sen apiece, at a time when the counter had traded around 60 sen earlier in the day.
He also offloaded two blocks of shares through his private vehicle Asia Internet Holdings Sdn Bhd on Aug 27 and 28. Some 4.29 million shares were disposed of on Aug 27 at 60.6 sen apiece, followed by another 52.3 million shares on Aug 28 at 48 sen apiece.
Over the two trading days, Wong and Asia Internet disposed of a total of RM57.5 million worth of shares as the stock tumbled.
However, it is unclear whether the disposals were part of the forced sale involving Wong's shares.
During an emergency conference call with analysts and investors, Wong acknowledged the margin pressure, saying he needed time to resolve the forced sales involving his accounts.
While Wong faced margin calls on his accounts, Zetrix is potentially sitting on millions of ringgit in paper losses on the shares it had repurchased so far this year. Zetrix's share price had not fallen below 60 sen before Aug 27.
The Main Market technology counter began 2026 at 81 sen and rose to a year-high of 89.5 sen on April 21, before gradually declining to trade between 68.5 sen and 79 sen in July.
When the company made its last purchase before the rout, Zetrix paid 66.5 sen apiece. The stock closed at 66 sen that day before falling 6.5 sen, or 9.85 per cent, to 59.5 sen on Aug 27.
VALUATION GAP WIDENS
Zetrix was already trading well below its historical valuation before the sell-off.
Based on its Aug 26 closing price of 66 sen, the stock's trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio stood at 5.3 times, a 62 per cent discount to its five-year average of 14 times, MyBursa data showed.
The P/E ratio measures how much investors are paying for each ringgit of a company's earnings. Zetrix's forward P/E of 4.7 times was also 65 per cent below its five-year average of 13.5 times.
The subsequent share-price collapse pushed that discount substantially wider.
By Aug 31, Zetrix's trailing P/E stood at 2.2 times, an 84 per cent discount to its five-year average of 13.9 times, while its forward P/E of 2.1 times was also 84 per cent below its five-year average of 13.4 times.
FROM 'BUY' CALL TO CUT-LOSS
Earlier in the month, when Zetrix closed one sen, or 1.42 per cent, higher at 71.5 sen on Aug 11, Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd issued a short-term "Buy" call on the stock.
It recommended an entry price of between 72 sen and 75 sen and set a target of 80.5 sen, saying early recovery signs were emerging at the time and the earlier downtrend appeared to be easing.
Its cut-loss level was set at 68 sen. By Aug 26, the stock had already fallen below that level, closing at 66 sen. Four trading sessions later, it was worth 22 sen — a decline of 44 sen, or 66.67 per cent.
Heavy selling in Zetrix shares came amid speculation linking the company to former human resources minister Datuk Seri M Saravanan, who was charged on Aug 28 with three counts of corruption involving RM1.097 million.
Zetrix categorically denied being implicated in or associated in any way with Saravanan in relation to the charges.
In its response to Bursa's UMA query, the company said it understood that what it described as "unfounded rumours or speculation" linking it to Saravanan may have contributed to the unusual trading activity.
It said enquiries with its directors, major shareholders and other relevant parties had not uncovered any undisclosed corporate development, including negotiations or discussions, that could account for the trading activity.
At the time of writing on Sept 3, Zetrix was the most actively traded stock as it entered its fifth straight day of decline, falling another 1.5 sen, or 6.82 per cent, to a multi-year low of 20.5 sen, with more than 209 million shares changing hands.
At that price, Zetrix had a market capitalisation of about RM1.65 billion, compared with roughly RM6.53 billion at 81 sen at the start of the year — a 74.7 per cent loss in market value.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gambling ban already Pas policy, no need for manifesto - Sanusi
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas does not need to include its opposition to gambling in its election manifesto as the stance is already enshrined in the party's Islamic principles, said Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor.
He said the party's position was clearly stated in Clause 5 of the Pas Constitution, which outlines its objective of upholding Islamic values and laws in governance, including the prohibition of gambling premises and regulation of alcohol sales.
Sanusi, who is also Pas election director said society should rely on their effort, prayer and tawakal (trust in God) to achieve success in life, rather than turning to gambling.
"I hope the people in this state and society as a whole will stay away from gambling activities and not rely on luck.
"Pas' position on the prohibition of gambling is clear and based on Islamic principles, and does not depend on whether the matter is listed in the election manifesto," he said to reporters at the sidelines of the 72nd Pas Muktamar.
Sanusi was responding to a video by Perlis Mufti Professor Datuk Dr Mohd Asri Zainul Abidin, who challenged Pas to include the issues of gambling and alcohol in its election manifesto.
The video was circulated by a portal's Facebook account.
Sanusi said there was no need to include such matters in the manifesto as the document was more of an offer by a political party to voters, rather than provisions already enshrined in the party's policies or constitution.
"People say a manifesto is not a holy book. Read the Pas Constitution — what does PAS stand for? But if people do not want Pas, they will still not want it, right? They will come up with all kinds of excuses.
"Islam prohibits gambling! Do we really need to put that in the manifesto too? Try reciting the syahadah (declaration of faith) as well," he said.
On developments concerning gambling premises in Kedah, Sanusi said the state government was still awaiting further action, including possible legal proceedings if gambling operators filed claims for compensation in court.
"We will wait for the next steps. (If) they want to take the matter to court to seek compensation, we will fight again," he said.

Title: FMM backs 3pct GST to cut manufacturers' tax burden
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturing (FMM) is pushing for a 3.0 per cent Goods and Services Tax (GST) as a way to ease tax-related cost pressures on manufacturers, but a tax expert said the proposed rate should be considered alongside its potential impact on government revenue.
FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said the proposed introductory rate, which is half the previous 6.0 per cent GST rate, would be a more acceptable starting point for businesses and consumers while giving manufacturers greater capacity to reinvest and improve productivity.
"We felt that a reasonable rate of three per cent would be more acceptable to the market.
"With the reduced GST burden of three per cent, I think the industry would have more capacity to undertake more productive manufacturing activities," Lee said at a press conference on Thursday.
The proposal forms part of FMM's wishlist for the 2027 Budget, alongside safeguards for essential consumption, simplified compliance for small and medium enterprises and reliable refund mechanisms.
FMM's push comes amid concerns over the cost implications of the current Sales and Services Tax (SST) regime.
According to FMM's Business Conditions Survey for the first half of 2026, 60 per cent of manufacturers reported higher production costs arising from embedded supply chain taxes, while 59 per cent cited unrecoverable taxes on business inputs.
Another 45 per cent reported compliance and administrative burdens, while 42 per cent pointed to uncertainty over the scope, exemptions and interpretation of SST.
Higher output costs were reported by 34 per cent of respondents, while 32 per cent cited reduced price competitiveness and 22 per cent faced cash flow pressures.
"SST is adding to manufacturers' costs through embedded and unrecoverable taxes, while administrative complexity and uncertainty compound the burden.
"The findings highlight the need to address tax cascading and simplify compliance to protect competitiveness and cash flow," Lee said.
BALANCING REVENUE AND EFFICIENCY
KPMG Malaysia head of tax Soh Lian Seng said the proposed 3.0 per cent rate is worth considering but should not be assessed in isolation.
He said the more important consideration was whether the structure could broaden the tax base, improve efficiency and generate sufficient revenue to support the government's fiscal position.
"While a three per cent GST rate may appear relatively modest compared with the current SST rates, it would be important to assess the net fiscal impact after taking into account the tax base, exemptions, registration thresholds, input tax credits and any changes to existing SST revenue.
"The government would need to ensure that any transition does not result in an unintended or significant erosion of revenue, taking into consideration the broader fiscal consolidation," Soh told Business Times.
GST has the advantage of being a more comprehensive and transparent consumption tax, with input tax credits helping to reduce tax cascading through the supply chain.
At the same time, the administrative and compliance implications, particularly for smaller businesses, would need to be carefully considered, he said.
The government had previously indicated that it was open to incorporating selected GST features into the existing SST framework to strengthen revenue collection without introducing a broad-based tax amid ongoing cost-of-living pressures.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said SST would remain the basis of the country's tax system, while features that could improve its efficiency and revenue collection could be considered.
FMM welcomed the government's position but called for systematic input tax credits or offsets, effective relief for essential goods and exports, and prompt refunds to reduce tax cascading, embedded production costs and cash flow pressures.
Soh said any move to incorporate selected GST features into SST should therefore focus on improving the credit mechanism and reducing cascading taxes while retaining some of the simplicity of SST.
"Rather than simply reverting to the previous GST model, we could potentially see a more streamlined consumption tax system that adopts the stronger features of both approaches. With that, we could consider calling it the Malaysian Consumption Tax," he said.
Ultimately, Soh said the objective should be to establish a consumption tax framework that is broad-based, efficient, transparent and fiscally sustainable, while keeping compliance requirements manageable for businesses.
"Any reform should strengthen, rather than weaken, the government's medium-term fiscal position," he added.

Title: Firm demand backs Bank Negara's 2.75pct OPR hold: experts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia's decision to keep the overnight policy rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent despite stronger economic growth reflects confidence that domestic demand remains firm without creating excessive inflationary or financial pressures, an economist said.
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia associate professor of property economics Dr Muhammad Najib Razali said the current policy stance gives the economy room to absorb external shocks while keeping borrowing costs supportive of household spending, business investment and infrastructure development.
"Strong gross domestic product (GDP) growth and resilient consumer spending are not, by themselves, reasons to raise interest rates.
"The more important issue is whether demand is creating persistent inflation, excessive borrowing, speculative asset-price increases, or instability in the ringgit," he told Business Times.
With headline and core inflation averaging 1.8 per cent and two per cent, respectively, in the first seven months of 2026, Najib said there was currently limited justification for an immediate tightening of monetary policy.
Bank Negara Malaysia yesterday maintained the OPR at 2.75 per cent at its fifth Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting of 2026, keeping the benchmark rate unchanged for a 14th consecutive month.
The central bank last cut the OPR by 25 basis points to 2.75 per cent in July 2025 as a pre-emptive measure to cushion growth against external headwinds.
Malaysia's economy expanded 5.7 per cent in the first half of 2026, prompting Bank Negara to expect full-year growth of around five per cent.
Najib said the strength of the economy was particularly encouraging because growth was increasingly supported by several engines rather than being dependent on a single source.
"Domestic consumption provides one stabilising pillar, while private and public investment provides another.
"Exports remain important, but Malaysia increasingly benefits from sectors linked to structural global demand, particularly semiconductors, electrical and electronics, machinery, digital infrastructure and artificial intelligence-related investment," he said.
He said keeping financing costs relatively low could also support the expansion of productive capacity, particularly through investment in transport, energy infrastructure, manufacturing, data centres and technology.
"This is different from simply stimulating household consumption. These investments increase productive capacity and potentially raise future productivity," he said.
The strategy could therefore strengthen Malaysia's resilience as the global economy faces a combination of tariff uncertainty, geopolitical conflict, energy-market disruptions and weaker global trade growth.
Najib said Malaysia could also benefit from the reorganisation of global supply chains as companies diversify production away from concentrated manufacturing locations.
Malaysia's established semiconductor ecosystem and position within Asean give it an opportunity to attract more investment, particularly if the country moves further into advanced packaging, chip design, testing and high-value manufacturing.
However, he cautioned that a relatively low OPR did not make Malaysia immune to external shocks.
"Malaysia remains a highly open economy. Strong domestic demand can cushion an external slowdown, but it cannot completely insulate the country from a major contraction in global trade," he said.
A prolonged US-China trade confrontation, a sharp downturn in semiconductor demand or a major global recession could still weigh on Malaysian exports, manufacturing and investment.
Energy prices pose another risk, particularly if prolonged conflict in the Middle East pushes global commodity prices higher and eventually feeds into domestic inflation.
"If geopolitical shocks begin to generate sustained inflation or financial instability, maintaining the same rate simply to support growth would become counterproductive," Najib said.
OPR COULD STAY AT 2.75PCT INTO 2027
Against the current backdrop, Najib expects Bank Negara to keep the OPR at 2.75 per cent until at least the end of this year and potentially through much of the first half of 2027.
"There is currently limited pressure for an immediate increase because inflation remains contained, household credit growth is moderate and the banking system remains stable," he said.
He expects the case for a rate hike to become stronger later in 2027 if inflation rises persistently, particularly if core inflation approaches three per cent, wage pressures intensify, household borrowing accelerates, property prices rise excessively or the ringgit comes under sustained pressure.
Under such conditions, he said Bank Negara could consider raising the OPR to three per cent.
Conversely, if inflation remains within the 1.5 to 2.5 per cent range and growth moderates towards a sustainable pace, there would be little reason for the central bank to tighten policy.
Najib said Malaysia's experience in 2017 and 2024 showed that Bank Negara was comfortable keeping rates unchanged even when economic growth was strong, provided inflation remained manageable.
He expects the OPR to remain at 2.75 per cent for another six to 12 months, with the possibility of a hike becoming more plausible in the second half of 2027 if inflationary pressures build.
Meanwhile, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the decision to maintain the OPR was broadly in line with expectations, including those of his team.
He said the accompanying statement also suggested that Bank Negara remained confident about the economy's growth prospects.
"The tone was fairly balanced and the positive macroeconomic condition is expected to continue in the remainder of the year," he said.
Afzanizam said the central bank's assessment pointed to Malaysia growing at a healthy pace of around five per cent in 2026, leaving little immediate need for a change in monetary policy.
"Hence, we believe the OPR is likely to be maintained at 2.75 per cent in the next MPC meeting in November," he said.
BIMB Securities Sdn Bhd analyst Zafri Zulkeffeli said the OPR was likely to remain at 2.75 per cent throughout 2026 and 2027, as policymakers await stronger domestic demand before resuming policy normalisation.
He said Malaysia's strong GDP growth had yet to translate into equally strong gains for households, with real gross national income lagging GDP by a record 3.8 percentage points in the second quarter of 2026.
"With
private consumption forecast below the 5.0 per cent mark and broadly in line with GDP
growth, there is little urgency to tighten monetary policy," he said.
Zafri said the disconnect was also evident in wages. Manufacturing sales rose 7.4 per cent year-on-year in the first half of 2026, while wages increased only 1.5 per cent, indicating that stronger corporate performance had yet to translate into comparable gains in household incomes.
He said OPR normalisation could re-emerge in 2028 if private consumption sustainably exceeds five per cent and outpaces overall economic growth, signalling firmer domestic demand.
On the external front, Zafri expects the US Federal Reserve to keep its federal funds rate unchanged for the rest of 2026 before resuming its easing cycle in 2027. The narrowing yield differential, together with lower US Treasury yields and relatively firmer Malaysian Government Securities yields, should support foreign inflows into Malaysian assets and provide a tailwind for the ringgit.
BIMB Securities forecasts the ringgit to average RM3.95 against the US dollar in 2026, RM3.90 in 2027 and RM3.85 in 2028.
JAPAN ADDS ANOTHER TEST
Meanwhile, rising Japanese government bond yields could create fresh competition for global capital.
Japan's 10-year yield breached three per cent on Tuesday, its highest since 1996, raising the prospect of capital being repatriated.
SPI Asset Management managing director Stephen Innes said this could pressure the ringgit if Malaysia's yield advantage narrows, while Tradeview Capital fund manager Neoh Jia Man warned of risks from an unwinding of the yen carry trade.
Still, the impact on Malaysia is expected to remain manageable given strong fundamentals.
The ringgit bond and sukuk market also reached a record RM2.388 trillion in August.
For Najib, the key to Malaysia's resilience is therefore not the 2.75 per cent OPR alone, but what the economy does with the breathing room provided by relatively low borrowing costs.
"The strategy can be summarised as domestic demand for stability, investment for capacity and diversified exports for growth.
"This combination should provide Malaysia with a stronger buffer against geopolitical and economic shocks than reliance on any single engine of growth," he said.

Title: Serian haze worsens, API hits 495
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions in Serian, Sarawak, have worsened, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) rising to 495 as of 7am today.
A check on the Department of Environment's (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) website found that Serian was the only area in the country to record a hazardous API reading above 300.
Three locations in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy API readings, with Kuching recording 289, followed by Samarahan (265) and Sri Aman (250).
Six other areas recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Sarikei (181), Sibu (174), Mukah (169), Bintulu (159), Samalaju (153) and ILP Miri (149).
It was reported that
cloud seeding operations
were being carried out in haze-hit areas, particularly those recording API readings above 150, as well as areas around dams where water levels were declining.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi was reported to have said the operations were being carried out in collaboration with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) and the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF).

Title: 'Zero updates': Families demand answers over missing Malaysians in Nepal [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Desperation has gripped the families of Malaysians still missing after the devastating  floods  in Nepal. They are now questioning the pace of the search-and-rescue  operation.
They want Wisma Putra to provide a clear account of the efforts under way, including where searches are being conducted, who is involved and what has been found, nine days after the disaster.
M. Subramaniam, 38, said families had repeatedly given authorities the names, photographs, personal details and last known locations of those missing, including his 74-year-old father-in-law, retired civil servant Krishnan Vadivelu.
"Zero updates so far. We have given the names and their last known locations. The information has been sent repeatedly, including to Wisma Putra and the relevant embassies, but until today, we still do not know anything," he said.
Subramaniam said the disaster has been particularly devastating for his wife, whose father had only recently begun adjusting to life following the death of his wife.
Subramaniam said Krishnan, a retired hospital attendant who lived alone in Perak, had expressed his wish to go on the pilgrimage to Mount Kailash. He joined the Spectrum Horizon tour group for this trip.
With his wife and other family members struggling to cope with the uncertainty, Subramaniam said he had taken on the responsibility of dealing with the authorities and coordinating with the other next of kin.
He said the family was prepared for any eventuality but could not accept being left without answers.
"But even if one person is found alive, that is something. We are hoping for miracles because we have no information.
"At the same time, we also have to face reality."
Subramaniam said some family members had travelled to Nepal to get information of their loved ones.
Among them was Hani Othman who has gone to look for her husband, Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, a Fire and Rescue Department officer.
He said the families had also heard unofficially through local contacts and tour operators that authorities might require more specialised personnel, including teams capable of recovering and identifying victims, rather than conventional search-and-rescue teams.
[[nid:1525355]]
Subramaniam said the families would continue pressing for verified information and greater coordination between Malaysia and the relevant authorities.
"We need facts. We need proper information. Nine days have passed, and the families deserve to know what has happened to their loved ones."
Dr R. Manivannan, whose younger sister Komathi Rethinam, 48, is missing, said the 26 victims from the Spectrum Horizon tour group were last known to have been at a building near the Tibet border when the disaster struck.
"Once they crossed, it was already considered Tibet," he said suggesting that Putrajaya's engagement with their Chinese counterparts was needed.
He acknowledged Malaysia could not simply enter another country's territory, but said diplomatic channels should be used to establish what happened.
He said immigration and border records should also be used to establish who crossed towards Tibet and when, potentially helping investigators reconstruct the missing travellers' movements.
"If people had crossed the border, there should be records somewhere. Even if a building was destroyed, immigration records do not simply disappear."
Dr Manivannan said police have started collecting DNA samples from next of kin who are still unaccounted for.
"Police came to our home in Cheras yesterday to collect DNA samples. Five family members provided samples, including our parents, the missing woman's child and two siblings."
He questioned why a comprehensive search-and-rescue operation had not been mounted earlier.
"Earlier we asked this on Day Four. We had hope. Now we have entered Day Nine."
The families also want hospitals, mortuaries and police stations systematically checked for unidentified victims, with officials using photographs and identifying information supplied by relatives.
Another family member, P. Sivan, 72, said his daughter Rajita, 47, did not show any change or give any message that could be considered as her last words before starting the journey.
He said he and Rajita's son dropped her off at Kuala Lumpur Sentral before she continued on to her destination.
"There was nothing strange before she left. She also did not send anything that we thought would be her last message.
"She is the eldest of two siblings and a very good child. She usually talks more to her mother, and even shares everything with her."
The Aug 26 flood has become one of the deadliest disasters to hit the Himalayan nation in recent years.
The huge wave of debris has killed more than 1,200 people and left more than 4,750 missing in Nepal and China's Tibet region, smashing towns, roads, bridges and multiple hydropower dams.
Putrajaya said 77 Malaysians have been found in Tibet and Nepal and brought to Kathmandu for repatriation.
However, 55 Malaysians remain unaccounted for.

Title: OpenAI begins rollout of new powerful AI model GPT-6 Astra
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: ChatGPT maker OpenAI said Thursday it would begin rolling out its newest and most powerful artificial intelligence (AI) model to select customers, saying it had built in safeguards to mitigate security risks.
"At this level of capability, safety has to become our top priority," OpenAI President Greg Brockman told reporters on a call about the release of GPT-6, also known as Astra.
Just over a year has passed since OpenAI launched the previous version of its flagship model, GPT-5.
Concerns about the capabilities of advanced models have grown since then, following incidents involving systems built by OpenAI and rival developer Anthropic.
OpenAI paused some model development for two weeks this summer after two models it was testing were involved in a security breach at AI platform Hugging Face.
The San Francisco-based company said Astra was developed with stronger safeguards after that incident, though Astra itself was not involved in the hack.
Some cybersecurity customers will get access to the new model Thursday, the company said, with a wider rollout to other paying customers to follow. Users on the free tier or the cheapest paid plan will not get access.
"We are working towards getting Astra in everyone's hands as quickly as we can; I know it is frustrating and I appreciate the patience. It should be quick," OpenAI CEO Sam Altman posted on social media Thursday afternoon.
In a blog post, OpenAI said Astra can autonomously handle a wide range of "tedious" computer tasks, including website creation, scientific analysis, game development, cybersecurity and coding.
To illustrate the time savings of building autonomous AI agents with Astra, the company said the model could cut apartment hunting from six hours to under 10 minutes.
"It's not unreasonable to feel that we are now in the AGI era," Brockman said on the call, referring to artificial general intelligence, a hypothetical stage at which AI systems match human intelligence across most tasks.
OpenAI previously had an agreement with Microsoft, one of its earliest and largest investors, under which an exclusivity clause would end once OpenAI reached AGI. Those terms were scrapped in April.
- 'Limited window' -
OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki acknowledged there was still uncertainty about how a new model behaves once released.
"A model can become very good at achieving a goal, and it can still act in ways that go against what the person intended," Pachocki said on the same call.
"We also have to be willing to slow down or withhold further scaling when our confidence in safety is not sufficient," he added.
Altman explained in an interview with Bloomberg TV on Thursday afternoon why the company decided to release a new model with this level of uncertainty and risk.
"The world is very close to a complete change in the landscape of cyber attacks, and the only way that we see for society to collectively defend itself... is to use tools like Astra to rapidly defend against these new cyber threats," Altman said.
In July OpenAI confirmed that it had reached one billion active users across all of its products, including both free and paid users.
OpenAI, Anthropic and more than 100 other organizations signed an open letter last week calling for a coordinated global response to AI-related cybersecurity risks, warning that the window to strengthen cyber defenses was limited.
Anthropic went further on Monday, calling for industry-wide coordination on safety and on the pace of developing increasingly capable models.
"I believe that shared safety standards and international coordination on further AI development need to be prioritized now," OpenIA's Pachocki said on Thursday.
The US state of Alabama opened an investigation into OpenAI last week over the Hugging Face breach, his office citing what it called the company's complete lack of oversight and adequate safeguards.
It also comes as OpenAI and rival Anthropic are both racing towards becoming public companies over the next several months, though OpenAI might not hold its IPO till sometime in 2027, according to reports.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: The rot has to stop: Time to end the plunder of the gravy train
Article:
IT has been quite an exhilarating time keeping up with all the goings-on in the courts these days.
We've seen everyone, from administrators, government agency directors, public-listed company chief executives and titled businessmen to political secretaries and even top army officials being escorted in and out of courtrooms for various offences.
Then, just when you thought you had seen it all, we had an unprecedented scenario where three former prime ministers ended up in the same court complex on the same day broadly to answer almost similar charges.
Who would have thought it possible, especially in a country where cynicism has become something of a national pastime?
One has been convicted of every graft charge brought against him and is now serving a prison sentence. Yet his legal battles are far from over, with almost daily court appearances to answer another long list of accusations.
The case against the latest former prime minister to be charged stemmed from the seizure last year of an estimated RM170 million in cash in various currencies and 16kg of gold worth nearly RM7 million from a residence and three safe houses.
He will, of course, have his day in court to explain the staggering amount of cash and gold in his possession leading up to the legal headache he is now facing.
Meanwhile, the third former leader, who ran the country for just 17 months between 2020 and 2021, is already making regular appearances in the Jalan Duta courtrooms to answer multiple corruption charges.
He, too, is fighting hard to dispel the prosecutors' accusations against him of soliciting millions in bribes from companies hoping to benefit from an emergency government spending programme.
And the parade to the dock has hardly stopped there.
A former minister has been charged over allegations he received RM1.1 million in kickbacks for approving foreign worker quotas.
Several C-suite executives have also been hauled in over yet more alleged shenanigans involving a government-owned Islamic financial institution that lost billions.
So, what is all this costing the country?
Previous reports indicate that an estimated RM277 billion was lost to corruption, systemic leakages and institutional fraud between 2018 and 2023.
[[nid:1525399]]
Zoom out further and the numbers become even more sobering. Think-tank models project total losses from cumulative corruption and its economic multiplier effects at as much as RM4.5 trillion over 26 years, from 1997 to 2022.
Transparency International Malaysia  and World Bank estimates paint an equally troubling picture.
Since 2013, Malaysia has been losing close to four per cent of its gross domestic product annually to corrupt practices.
That figure rose from two per cent in 2010 to four per cent in 2013.
Whatever way you slice it, the country has been paying a staggering price.
The natural question is: is anything being done about it?
If anything, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) seems to be springing into action.
This year alone, it has pursued a sweeping range of corruption, money laundering and criminal breach of trust cases involving the military, financial institutions, government-linked companies and corporate figures.
In other words, the net must be cast wide. We are also hearing promises of zero tolerance towards the plundering of the nation's wealth.
No less that the prime minister himself has made it clear that he intends to end the plundering of the national gravy train once and for all, pledging action against those involved regardless of rank, position or political affiliation.
For the rest of us, there is little choice but to support the crackdown on those bleeding the country dry.
There is a need to continue asking the tough questions, especially how some people are accumulating an astronomical amount of wealth that ordinary Malaysians struggle to build across generations?
The burning question, however, is one we have avoided for far too long.
With the vast wealth of oil, gas, palm oil, rubber, timber, agricultural resources and so much else going for us, why have we struggled to keep pace with regional neighbours blessed with far fewer natural advantages?
Truth be told, Malaysia was built to succeed. We have natural wealth, a strategic location, and a diverse and capable population. And, compared with many of our neighbours, relative freedom from catastrophic natural disasters.
We have had almost every advantage. Yet somewhere along the way, corruption became one of the biggest anchors dragging us down.
That is the uncomfortable truth we must confront. For decades, we have watched scandals erupt, inquiries launched, committees formed and promises made. Then, too often, the noise fades and it is back to business as
usual.
That cycle must end. Enough of the excuses. Enough of the grand promises followed by silence and selective outrage.
The rot has gone on for far too long. It is time to stop it and get the country back on track for the betterment of all Malaysians.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran war is not a war, US VP Vance says
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Vice President JD Vance said Thursday he would not categorise the Iran war as a war, despite continuing clashes with Teheran six months after the start of the conflict.
Vance's comments came amid growing signs that President Donald Trump is trying to draw a line under the conflict that has bogged down his administration.
"I wouldn't call it a war. Right now, there is no active shooting," Vance told a White House briefing when asked if the war would be over by US midterm elections in November.
Vance added that "I recognise there have been places where this has flared up" but said major combat operations only lasted for six weeks after the US-Israel war started on Feb 28.
"But when you ask when will this end, you're asking me a question like when will the Iranians stop shooting at ships? I think the reality is I don't know the answer to that question. You would have to ask the Iranians," he said.
After several weeks of calm, fresh clashes began with US raids on Sunday, deepening the impasse in the six-month war, as Iran maintains a stranglehold on the strategic Strait of Hormuz.
Vance insisted that the United States would not reopen talks with Iran until it ended attacks on commercial shipping.
But with fuel prices threatening to cost Trump's Republicans their control of Congress at the ballot box, his administration has begun pushing the message that oil flows through the waterway are now returning to pre-war levels.
WEDDING STRIKE PROBE
"Their control over the Strait of Hormuz is effectively gone," Vance said of Iran.
"If you go back three months ago, how much oil and gas was coming out of the strait under Iranian threats? It was virtually nothing. Now, it's almost back to where it was before the conflict even started," Vance said.
Trump's approval ratings are near record lows as the president who vowed to keep the United States out of any more foreign wars finds himself in a quagmire with the Islamic republic.
Eighteen US troops and thousands of people in Iran and Lebanon have died in the conflict since February.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump was now discussing with senior aides about whether to declare the Iran war over. He posted a photo of a banner saying "Mission Accomplished" last week.
Iran pressed on with fresh attacks on Thursday, saying it hit US military bases in Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates to avenge a strike on a wedding that it blamed on Washington.
Vance said the United States was probing the wedding strike but cast doubt on Iranian reporting of the incident.
"I know that we're investigating," Vance said. "I will say that the Iranian state media has not been a very good scribe about what's happened in the conflict thus far. So I'm extremely skeptical of this."
The Iranian Red Crescent said the missile attack on the wedding in the Iranian coastal town of Kuhestak killed four people late Tuesday, including a child, and wounded more than 50.

Title: 20 students find journalism spark during Media Prima visit
Article:

ABOUT 20 Kolej Profesional Mara Seri Iskandar students visited Media Prima Bhd yesterday, where they gained first-hand exposure to newsroom and broadcasting operations.
The Diploma in English Communication students visited Balai Berita under Eduscape, an initiative by Media Prima aimed at exposing students to television, radio, print and digital media operations.
Led by News and Current Affairs (NCA) Production Support and Technical Operations manager Abdul Rahim Daim, the tour covered Media Prima Audio, NCA studios, Rev Media Group and the editorial floor of the 'New Straits Times', 'Berita Harian' and 'Harian Metro'.
The students took turns anchoring news at the studio.
Adam Iskandar Ardi Suhairi, 18, from Kuala Terengganu, said it opened his eyes to the work done behind what audiences see and hear every day.
"I found the visit really fun. It was very interactive and interesting.
"I never knew there was so much thought behind everything, from the radio station to the news anchors," he said.
The visit also sparked an interest in broadcast journalism among some students.
Adibah Raihanah Rahman, 19, from Tawau, said she was particularly drawn to news reading.
"I'm interested in journalism, especially news reading. It feels surreal. I sat on the news anchor's chair and read the teleprompter by myself.
"I think that's such a beautiful experience and I would like to experience it again," said Adibah.
Nurul Adawiyah Mohd Amli, 19, shared a similar aspiration.
"I'm interested in becoming a newsreader because I think I have the talent for it," she said.

Title: 40 wild elephants roaming forests near Pos Gob
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
ABOUT 40 wild elephants are believed to be roaming the forests around Pos Gob, where their natural migration routes overlap with nearby settlements.
Kelantan Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) director Wan Mohd Adib Wan Yusoh said the elephants were part of the ID Nenggiri herd.
"The elephants may appear at any time as they move through the forest in search of food.
"With parts of human settlements being close to their natural routes, the elephants can pose a risk if approached or are provoked," he said.
On Aug 24, a fully grown wild male elephant approached the Kembara Rakyat Nenggiri programme campsite in Pos Gob at 4am, startling about 150 participants.
The encounter has renewed concerns over human-elephant conflict in the remote Orang Asli settlement, which lies within the Balah Permanent Forest Reserve.
Wan Mohd Adib said Perhilitan would deploy officers to monitor the area.
He urged the public to stay away from wild elephants or to sound vehicle horns or shine lights to chase them away.
Meanwhile, Universiti Malaysia Kelantan lecturer Associate Professor Dr Kamarul Ariffin Kambali @ Hambali said land clearing, expansion of plantations and the Nenggiri dam project could further disrupt elephant habitats and drive the animals closer to human settlements.
He proposed establishing food banks inside the forest, as well as electric fencing or sandbag barriers, to reduce encounters between elephants and local communities.
Nenggiri assemblyman Mohd Azmawi Fikri Abdul Ghani said wildlife conflicts in Pos Gob had persisted for two years and called for a comprehensive solution to protect residents.

Title: Penang bags RM17.3b in approved manufacturing investments
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
GEORGE TOWN: Penang led Malaysia in approved manufacturing investments in the first half of this year, securing RM17.3 billion, according to the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida).
The figure represented a 38 per cent year-on-year increase from the corresponding period last year, with the state accounting for 34 per cent of Malaysia's total approved manufacturing investments during the six-month period.
Of the total, RM12.8 billion came from foreign direct investment (FDI), accounting for 74 per cent of Penang's approved manufacturing investments and 39 per cent of the country's total manufacturing FDI.
Hong Kong, Singapore, China and the United States were the top investors, collectively accounting for 77 per cent of the state's approved manufacturing FDI.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state's investment performance, despite geopolitical tensions and global economic uncertainties, reflected the strength and resilience of its established industrial ecosystem.
"Moving forward, our industrial strategy is centred on three key priorities," he said at his office in Komtar here yesterday.
"The first priority is to continue attracting strategic investments and technologies that complement and strengthen Penang's established ecosystem.
"Subsequently, it is to enable local companies' active participation in the global value chain through encouraging localisation by multinational corporations, and to develop an AI-ready ecosystem and talent to drive innovation and competitiveness."
Chow thanked investors for their continued confidence in Penang, as well as Mida, InvestPenang, Penang Development Corp, and other federal and state agencies for their collaboration in strengthening the state's business environment.
Penang also recorded RM4.5 billion in approved manufacturing domestic direct investment, a 125 per cent increase year-on-year, reflecting continued investment by local companies.
Investment activity was concentrated in the state's promoted electrical and electronics, and machinery and equipment sectors, which collectively accounted for 88 per cent of total approved manufacturing investments.
Expansion projects made up RM11.9 billion, or 69 per cent, while new projects accounted for RM5.4 billion, or 31 per cent. The investments involved 177 projects and are expected to create 19,337 new jobs.
A significant portion of the approved investments is expected to position Penang to capture opportunities arising from the AI wave, strengthening its capabilities across the AI value chain.

Title: '800 ill in latest Indonesian food poisoning outbreaks'
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
NEARLY 800 Indonesians have fallen ill in separate incidents of food poisoning linked to the government's free meals programme, said a member of a parliamentary commission overseeing health, including more than 500 students in East Java province this week.
President Prabowo Subianto launched his multibillion-dollar programme last year to eradicate under-nutrition by giving free meals to tens of millions of children, but the scheme has been dogged by controversies, including mass food poisoning, allegations of corruption, leadership changes and a burdensome price tag.
Aside from the 512 students who fell ill in the region of Sidoarjo in East Java, 49 suffered from poisoning in the East Java city of Nganjuk and 237 in the West Sumatra region of Agam, said Charles Honoris, a lawmaker and member of the sole political party outside the governing coalition, on Instagram on Wednesday.
Charles cited local health department data to make the claim and said they were not isolated incidents.
"This is a failure of the system," he said.
The National Nutrition Agency, which oversees the US$12.94 billion programme, did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the lawmaker's post.
It suspended the kitchen linked to the Sidoarjo case on Wednesday.
There have been a number of outbreaks of mass food poisoning linked to the free-meals scheme, with 37,600 individuals reported to have been affected as of Aug 8, according to Network for Education Watch, a non-governmental watchdog.
Improper food storage and late delivery of cooked meals are often to blame for the food poisoning, authorities have said.
In July, a survey by pollster Saiful Mujani Research and Consulting showed only one-third of people were satisfied with the scheme, with the reported cases of poisoning cited as a major reason. — REUTERS

Title: Ahead of elections, Israel tests West's patience on West Bank violence
Article:
ISRAEL'S ties with many Western allies were already fraught over its conduct in the Gaza war, but the worsening situation in the occupied West Bank has seen relations nosedive before close-fought October elections.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing government is pushing ahead with the expansion of Israeli settlements, which are illegal under international law, while daily reports of settler attacks against Palestinians provoke international outrage.
While many observers expect caution from Western states in their responses before the elections, Britain's foreign secretary on Tuesday vowed a major policy reset towards Israel's West Bank construction and promised a "comprehensive set of measures" within weeks.
France's foreign minister also urged the European Union to ban trade with settlements, calling surging West Bank violence "an unacceptable affront to the dignity of the Palestinian people."
A Tel Aviv-based European diplomat told AFP that the idea of taking measures against Israel once seemed "completely unthinkable."
"Obviously, the dial has shifted over time," he added, requesting anonymity to speak on the sensitive matter.
"The West Bank we're very, very concerned about," he said. "There seems to be a huge, unprecedented level of settler violence. It doesn't look like the authorities are taking efforts to deal with that as seriously as we'd like."
Another European diplomat based in Jerusalem said there was political will to preserve a two-state solution, with Israel seen as crossing most red lines in making a Palestinian state unviable.
"Without an outright 'we are annexing the West Bank' announcement, I don't know what further red lines there are," he told AFP, also requesting anonymity.
Observers say the UK's measures are likely to target individuals and organisations directly involved in Israeli settlement expansion, rather than broader sanctions.
Israel has fought against foreign governments making any distinction between goods from Israel and West Bank settlements.
A British ban on trade with settlements "economically, in isolation... is relatively small", said Andreas Krieg, an associate professor at King's College London.
But he said the regulatory impact and precedent it sets would be important.
"If Britain, France, Germany and other European economies begin converging around the same principle, it becomes much more consequential," he told AFP.
While the United States provides Israel with crucial diplomatic and military support, the EU is Israel's biggest trading partner, according to the European Commission.
[[nid:1525295]]
Several EU countries – including Ireland, the Netherlands and Spain – have imposed their own settlement trade restrictions.
But getting bloc-wide measures over the line requires securing agreement across EU member states.
In August, Slovenia's new right-wing government reportedly opposed an EU-wide condemnation of Israel's E1 settlement project that would undermine the contiguity of any future Palestinian state, downgrading the bloc's response.
But the Israeli elections are likely to delay any major European announcements, over fears of interference accusations or galvanising Netanyahu's right-wing base.
"There's a worry that if they push too hard against Israel right now, it'll feed into what's sometimes called the siege mentality that Netanyahu often speaks to," said Julie Norman, an expert at Chatham House think tank.
All the while, Israel's ties with traditional allies continue to fray, exacerbated by ever-inflammatory rhetoric from officials.
"We had a difficult relationship with this current administration anyway," the Tel Aviv-based European diplomat told AFP.
"But it seems to us like now it's very much a policy, certainly in the run-up to the elections, that we seem to be fair game," he added.
"There is damage being done to that relationship by some of the rhetoric coming out of certain ministries and by what's happening in the West Bank."
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said in June he was severing all contact with the EU's top diplomat after she allegedly compared Israel to apartheid-era South Africa.
In response to Britain's pledge of anti-settlement measures, Saar has vowed retaliation without elaborating, with Israel reportedly looking at expelling diplomats.
A former Israeli diplomat in Europe told AFP he felt Saar's threat was an "empty gun", but said that Israel's ties with Europe in general had deteriorated under Netanyahu's watch.
The EU-Israel relationship is "on hold" until after elections, he said.
"We won't see any dramatic movement from the side of the European Union and the member states, everyone is waiting for the results, everyone I think is hoping that there will be a change."
* The writers are from AFP

Title: Thailand scraps 60-day visa-free entry, reinstates 30-day scheme
Article:
BANGKOK: Thailand will implement a major overhaul of its tourist visa exemption and visa‑on‑arrival rules from Sept 15, officially ending the 60‑day exemption scheme introduced two years ago, the Foreign Ministry announced.
Under the revised framework approved by Cabinet, Thailand will reintroduce a 30‑day visa‑free entry scheme, introduce a new 15‑day exemption category for select countries, and restructure the visa‑on‑arrival list.
Department of Consular Affairs director‑general Mungkorn Pratoomkaew said immigration data showed the average stay for foreign tourists is under 15 days, making the blanket 60‑day exemption redundant.
He explained that national security, curbing transnational crime, economic benefits and diplomatic reciprocity guided the recalibration.
Between 20 and 30 countries were excluded from the revised list after authorities assessed inbound visitor numbers and reciprocal privileges for Thai passport holders.
According to the Royal Gazette, the revised 30‑day exemption applies to ordinary passport holders from 60 countries and territories. A new 15‑day exemption covers travellers from two countries, while visa‑on‑arrival is narrowed to three nations.
Existing bilateral visa‑waiver agreements with 16 countries remain unaffected.
Mungkorn noted that tourists arriving before midnight Sept 14 will retain their permitted stay under current rules, including the 60‑day entry stamp.
Travellers seeking longer stays under the new regime must apply for a standard 60‑day tourist visa via the global e‑visa system, though in‑country extensions remain available.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia rescues 11 orangutans as wildfire approaches rehabilitation centre
Article:
JAKARTA:  Eleven orangutans were evacuated from a rehabilitation centre in East Kalimantan as forest fires closed in, Indonesian authorities confirmed, activating emergency measures to protect the endangered primates.
Ari Wibawanto, head of the East Kalimantan Natural Resources Conservation Agency (BKSDA), said emergency status was declared at the Jejak Pulang Forest School in Samboja, Kutai Kartanegara regency, on Sept 1 after smoke and flames began approaching.
The orangutans undergoing rehabilitation were moved to a temporary care facility.
"Post‑evacuation checks showed that all 11 orangutans were healthy and safe from smoke exposure," Ari said.
He added that rehabilitation continues at the temporary facility through feeding, activities and enrichment programmes to maintain their health and natural behaviour.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesian police bust online gambling network generating US$56.6mil annually
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesian police have dismantled a multimillion‑rupiah online gambling network operating three overseas‑based websites, arresting five suspects in a crackdown that exposed transactions worth more than 1 trillion rupiah (about US$56.6 million) annually.
National Police cybercrime director Adex Yudiswan said the websites were controlled from overseas but operated in Indonesia and other countries.
The five suspects, arrested in July in Jakarta, South Tangerang and Semarang, allegedly helped set up a shell company and open bank accounts to collect gambling proceeds.
Police said the network processed over 1.03 trillion rupiah in transactions between January and August, averaging 8.6 billion rupiah daily. Authorities have frozen about 51 billion rupiah held by five payment service providers.
Investigators are searching for a sixth suspect believed to have directed the operation.
The suspects face up to 15 years in prison under Indonesia's electronic fund transfer and criminal laws.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three killed after jumping from burning factory in Indonesia
Article:
JAKARTA:  Three construction workers plunged to their deaths after leaping from the sixth floor of a burning soap factory in Indonesia's North Sumatra province on Thursday, local police confirmed.
The fire broke out around 10am at the Evyap Sabun Indonesia factory in the Sei Mangkei Special Economic Zone, Simalungun regency, police spokesperson Verry Purba said.
The victims, aged 26 to 43, were welding assistants working for a contractor. They jumped when flames and smoke reached their work area and an explosion‑like sound was heard.
All three were rushed to hospital but died from injuries sustained in the fall.
Preliminary information indicated the blaze began on the third or fourth floor. Firefighters were still battling the flames more than three hours later, while the cause remained under investigation.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno must choose government or quit if it favours PN, says PKR Youth leader
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A PKR Youth leader has challenged Umno to either commit to the unity government or relinquish its positions in the government if the party is in favour of Perikatan Nasional.
PKR Youth deputy chief Nabil Halimi said Umno should not be seen as having one foot in the unity government while simultaneously cooperating with the opposition.
Nabil also challenged Umno ministers and Members of Parliament to clearly state their position if they believe the 16th General Election (GE16) should be held earlier to obtain a fresh mandate from the people.
"If they want to remain with the government, then remain and shoulder the responsibility until the mandate is completed.
"If they want to join PN, then make that decision and relinquish their positions in the government.
"Umno should not be seen as having one foot in the government and the other in the opposition, embracing PN at the state level while still wanting to enjoy positions and posts in the Madani government in Putrajaya," he said in a Facebook post.
Nabil added that the people should not be made to feel confused by such political manoeuvring.
"The people's mandate is not a bargaining tool for political negotiations. Let the people make their assessment when the time comes for an election," he said.
In an interview with Media Prima Bhd recently, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also Barisan Nasional chairman, had said that he supported an
early GE16
.
He said this would allow the government to seek a fresh mandate.
During the Johor election in June, PN urged its supporters not to vote for Pakatan Harapan in seats the coalition did not contest. This included seats that saw straight fights between PH and BN.
In the Negri Sembilan polls, BN and PN entered into an electoral pact, with the two coalitions subsequently securing more than a two-thirds majority and forming the state government together.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mechanic injured after gunmen open fire at workshop
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: A 43-year-old mechanic was injured in his right palm after being shot at by two men at a car workshop in Jalan Sungai Lembu here yesterday.
It is learnt that at least three shots were fired at the victim in the 1.45pm incident.
The victim was reportedly approached by two men on a motorcycle while he was at the workshop before they opened fire.
He then ran about 50 metres from the workshop and jumped over a fence opposite a Chinese cemetery to escape.
The victim is believed to have lodged a police report with the Kulim police station in Kedah before being sent to hospital for treatment.
Police are investigating the motive and said the victim has a previous criminal record.
Earlier, police and forensic personnel found bullets and spent cartridges at the scene.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng, when contacted, confirmed the incident.
"Efforts to track down the suspects are underway," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 307 of the Penal Code for attempted murder.

Title: 12-year-old boy killed in Gurun crash involving motorcycle, two lorries
Article:
GURUN: A 12-year-old boy was killed in an accident involving a motorcycle and two lorries at Masjid Batu 3, Jalan Jeniang, here today.
The Kedah Fire and Rescue Department Operations Centre (PGO) said it received a distress call via the NG999 line at 1.36pm.
Based on information from the caller, a victim was trapped under a lorry, prompting the PGO to dispatch an LFRT fire engine and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) vehicle from the Guar Chempedak Fire and Rescue Station to the scene.
"The accident involved a tar-loaded lorry and a motorcycle, while a trailer was parked on the road shoulder near the scene.
"The 12-year-old victim was believed to be trapped under the lorry and sustained serious injuries, while another 14-year-old boy survived.
"The victim was pronounced dead by a Health Ministry medical officer before his body was handed over to police for further action," it said.
Firefighters later carried out clean-up work at the scene to ensure the area was safe and secure.
The operation ended at 3.59pm.
