Title: El Nino could be strongest in four decades, UN warns
Article:
GENEVA: El Nino is forecast to be the strongest since comparable records began four decades ago, the United Nations' climate agency warned Thursday, with the UN chief saying the world was in the "danger zone of extreme weather."
The weather phenomenon is set to become "very strong" in the months ahead and is near certain to persist through to February, the World Meteorological Organization said.
"If this trajectory continues, it may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began," WMO chief Celeste Saulo told reporters in Geneva.
El Nino will peak towards the end of this year – though its knock-on impacts for the climate will continue well into 2027, said the WMO.
El Nino warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, bringing worldwide changes in winds, pressure and rainfall.
Heat in the oceans releases more slowly into the atmosphere, pushing up global temperatures the year after it develops.
The powerful 2023-24 El Nino contributed to 2024 being the warmest year on record, and "we should not be surprised if this record is broken", Saulo added.
"El Nino is firmly established and will intensify into a very strong event in the coming months, with big impacts on rainfall and temperature patterns and associated risks of floods, drought and extreme heat," the WMO said.
- HIGHWAY TO THE DANGER ZONE -
El Nino is a naturally-occurring phenomenon and is not caused by climate change.
But scientists expect it will exacerbate the heat of a planet already warming from burning fossil fuels, while amping up weather extremes.
"El Nino is being supersized before our eyes," said UN chief Antonio Guterres.
"The science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up. Sea surface temperatures are rising, temperatures keep climbing, and the world is in the danger zone of extreme weather."
WMO chief Saulo urged disaster management authorities and climate-sensitive sectors like agriculture, fisheries health, energy and water to prepare themselves.
"This exceptional El Nino... has the potential to deliver a massive blow to communities and economies across the world", she said.
"We are already seeing disruption and devastation from droughts and floods, and we expect these impacts to increase as El Nino intensifies."
El Nino typically takes place every two to seven years and lasts around nine to 12 months.
Conditions oscillate between El Nino and its opposite La Nina, with neutral conditions in between.
El Nino can reshape weather and climate patterns thousands of kilometres away from the tropical Pacific.
- PACIFIC OCEAN HEATING UP -
Wilfran Moufouma-Okia, the WMO's climate prediction chief, said some places would be affected before, some during and some after the peak later this year – though the strength of the peak is not an indicator of the severity of the impact.
For September-November, WMO forecasts indicate an increased likelihood of above-normal temperatures "across almost all land areas."
The index which measures sea surface temperature anomalies in the central eastern equatorial Pacific has strengthened from an average 1.5C above normal between May and July.
Weekly values between late July and mid-August ranged from around 2.2C to 2.6C above average, indicating continued El Nino intensification.
The UN agency classifies El Nino events as weak, moderate, strong or very strong – meaning this one is set to reach the highest level out of four.
Moufouma-Okia said the classification meant a sea surface temperature anomaly of more than plus 2C.
"That category is open: we know where it starts; we don't know where it ends," he told AFP.
The average forecast is pointing towards an anomaly peaking at plus 3.6C – way higher than the last two very strong El Ninos in 1997-98 and 2015-16.
In some areas, sub-surface ocean temperatures were more than 8C above average during July and early August.
Saulo called this a huge reservoir of "very warm ocean waters that will fuel the intensity of El Nino."
The UN's International Organization for Migration agency appealed Thursday for US$110 million to protect 4.9 million people from the potentially severe impacts of the phenomenon.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TVET student missing while catching crabs found drowned
Article:
MELAKA: A teenage boy who went missing at Pantai Klebang while catching crabs with friends yesterday was found floating near Pulau Upeh today.
The victim, 16-year-old TVET student Muhammad Arif Daniel Nizamuddin, was found at 7.20pm, about two nautical miles from the shore.
Melaka Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Mohd Shahrom Laji said the victim was identified by his family at 8.30pm.
He said the search and rescue (SAR) operation began yesterday, with the department's Water Rescue Team conducting a solo search around the area where the teenager was last seen.
"Searches were also conducted between rocks along the shoreline, while the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) searched the waters.
"Firefighters also used the arc-pattern search technique about 30 metres from the shoreline," he said in a statement today.
He said the victim's body was handed over to police for further action.
The operation involved 25 personnel from the Melaka Tengah Fire and Rescue Department, with assistance from the Masjid Tanah Fire and Rescue Station, MMEA and the police.
Yesterday, it was reported
that a group of teenagers' outing
to catch rock crabs turned tragic when one of them went missing at the sea wall at Pantai Klebang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lebanon receives first detainee of five to be freed by Israel
Article:
BEIRUT: Lebanon said it received a man on Thursday freed as Israel announced it would release five people seized from the country's south, where it has fought several wars against Iran-backed Hizbollah in recent years.
The announcement came after Lebanon said its army received a man returned by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the first since Beirut called in August talks for the release of an initial group seized since the start of a 2024 Israel-Hizbollah war.
"It was decided to release five Lebanese civilians who were arrested in areas under (Israeli army) control in southern Lebanon," the office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a statement.
"After their interrogation was completed, it became clear that they are civilians who are not members of any terrorist organisation, have not engaged in terrorism, and there is no reason to continue holding them in Israel."
Lebanese authorities have not officially announced the number of citizens Israel seized during that war and a subsequent 2026 conflict, but a list of more than 30 people has been compiled by their families and a committee working on their cases.
The list includes at least one Syrian national and several Hizbollah fighters.
Netanyahu's office said the decision followed "extensive efforts" by Israel and Lebanon to locate and return the bodies of leaders of Lebanon's Jewish community abducted and killed in the 1980s during the country's 15-year civil war.
After the latest round of Lebanon-Israel talks in Rome last month, a Lebanese official said Israel gave Beirut a list of individuals to demand the return of their remains.
The Israeli military said in August it recovered the remains of a soldier killed in eastern Lebanon in 1982.
- 'HUMANITARIAN OPERATION' -
The ICRC, which handles the transfer of released people between Israel and Lebanon, said a humanitarian operation was underway.
Lebanon's state-run National News Agency said that the Lebanese army received Malek Ghazi earlier on Thursday, adding that he was taken to an army intelligence headquarters in the southern city of Tyre.
Ghazi's family, from the southeastern town of Ain Ata, said in October last year that they had lost contact with him after he had gone out to exercise.
Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam hailed the release in a statement, thanking "the American administration... for the efforts exerted in this regard."
He pledged to work "until the release of all our prisoners" and "the disclosure of the fate of the missing", as well as an Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory.
Hizbollah attacked Israel in 2023 in support of Hamas after the outbreak of the Gaza war, leading to over a year of hostilities that escalated into a full-blown war in 2024.
The group drew Lebanon into the Middle East war two years later in support of its backer Iran after launching rockets at Israel.
Israel responded with airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people.
The conflict has calmed since a US-Iran memorandum of understanding and a framework agreement between Israel and Lebanon agreed in June.
The Lebanon-Israel deal calls for the disarmament of Hizbollah, a gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from south Lebanon and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the region, starting in "pilot zones."
A date has not yet been set for the next round of Lebanon-Israel talks, and Israel still carries out strikes on Lebanon while occupying parts of its territory.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar vows to strengthen MITRA and expand Indian community support
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — The Indian community will not be sidelined in the national development agenda, with the Madani government continuing to expand efforts to improve the community’s standard of living, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the efforts included widening access to financing for entrepreneurs, strengthening the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra), enhancing entrepreneurship and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), and creating more opportunities for youth development through mentor-mentee programmes.
“Various efforts have been undertaken in education, entrepreneurship, microfinancing, welfare and cash assistance to ease the burden on families and improve their standard of living,” he said in a Facebook post last night.
Anwar today continued his engagement sessions with Indian community leaders to review progress in implementing the Madani government’s agenda, while listening to their views and concerns that remain unresolved.
He said the remaining gaps, including those related to poverty, citizenship and access to assistance, must be addressed promptly and effectively.
The prime minister also urged the relevant ministries and agencies to strengthen synergy and streamline service delivery to ensure every allocation and policy implemented reaches its intended target groups and brings about tangible improvements in the lives of the people. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak haze pushes Serian API reading to 495, just short of ‘emergency’ level
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 4 — Haze in Serian worsened sharply overnight, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) there climbing to 495 this morning, just five points below the level that would trigger an “emergency” declaration.
The Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) recorded the reading at the Serian monitoring station at 7am today, making it the only locality in the country with a hazardous reading.
The reading began rising from 6pm yesterday after haze conditions had shown signs of improvement over the preceding 24 hours.
Three other areas in Sarawak were in the very unhealthy category, with API readings of 289 in Kuching, 265 in Samarahan and 250 in Sri Aman.
Eight other localities, including two in Sabah, recorded unhealthy readings below 200.
Sarawak Disaster Management Committee chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas previously said a locality would be declared an emergency if its API reading reached 500.
Such a declaration would result in the closure of all public and private sector activities except essential services, he said.
The Sarawak Disaster Management Committee would then notify the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) in Kuala Lumpur for further action.

Title: Nepal tragedy: Support group seeks Tamil counsellors for victims’ families
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Solidariti Malaysia: Keluarga Dalam Harapan (MASFIH), a support group for families of victims in the Nepal flash flood tragedy, has appealed for certified Tamil-speaking counsellors to provide psychological support to affected relatives.
MASFIH representative Dr R. Manivannan said Tamil-speaking counsellors were urgently needed as most of the next of kin were elderly individuals who were only comfortable communicating in their mother tongue.
He noted that while Wisma Putra and Mercy Malaysia proactively offered free counselling services, the initiative faced language barriers as sessions were conducted in Malay and English.
He said using third-party translators during therapy sessions was unsuitable as it could affect the emotional connection families needed during this difficult time.
“Translators may be available, but a third party’s presence might make the families uncomfortable, and the counsellor’s true intent or nuance might not get across to them,” he said.
“Therefore, if there are government or private counsellors fluent in Tamil, we welcome them to contact us so that the screening process can be coordinated with Mercy Malaysia or Wisma Putra,” he told a press conference on the Nepal-Tibet flash flood incident here yesterday.
Meanwhile, he advised families to monitor the emotional state of their immediate relatives to ensure those experiencing trauma received proper screening.
“The families themselves must come forward. Other family members need to be attentive because everyone copes with trauma differently,” he said.
Commenting on the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) expected to deploy to Nepal this Saturday, Manivannan welcomed the effort, saying it would ensure more accurate on-the-ground information.
“At least when Smart arrives, we will receive first-hand updates from our own Malaysian personnel, which will be more accurate and hopefully pave the way for victims’ families to go there later,” he said.
Manivannan’s younger sister, R. Komathi, 48, is among the Malaysians reported missing in the incident. — Bernama

Title: Lim Guan Eng calls for Penang fee, quit rent and water tariff hikes to be deferred
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — DAP’s Air Putih assemblyman Lim Guan Eng has urged the Penang government to emulate Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim by deferring increases in fees, quit rent and water tariffs to ease the financial burden on businesses and households.
Lim said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow and state executive councillor Zairil Khir Johari should adopt the same reformist approach and political will to fulfil the election manifesto and ease the cost of living for Penang residents.
He said many landowners in Penang were struggling to cope with sharply higher quit rent this year, particularly amid an uncertain economic outlook and rising fuel prices linked to the US-Iran conflict.
“Chow Kon Yeow should defer all increases until the global economy and its outlook become stable again,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Lim also criticised Zairil for refusing to support a postponement of the 20-sen increase in the water tariff per cubic metre, which took effect on July 1.
He said the increase would generate an additional RM20 million a year for Perbadanan Bekalan Air Pulau Pinang (PBAPP), but would have a negative impact on 1.8 million Penang residents.
Lim cited PBAPP’s financial results, saying its pre-tax profit more than doubled from RM23.1 million in the first quarter of 2025 to RM49.6 million in the same period this year.
He said PBAPP’s RM49.6 million pre-tax profit for the first three months of 2026 was already more than double the RM20 million in additional annual revenue expected from the tariff increase.
“Therefore, if the water tariff increase is deferred for one year, PBAPP should be able to withstand it financially,” he said.
Lim added that should PBAPP urgently require the RM20 million, the state government could seek a federal grant or loan instead.
He questioned why the federal government would reject such assistance, claiming Putrajaya owed Penang RM2.8 billion after returning only RM7.9 billion of the RM10.7 billion contributed by the state between 2023 and 2025.
“Where there is a will, there is a way; as long as the state government continues to put the people first rather than PBA Holdings Bhd,” he said.

Title: Ramanan: PM discussed Budget 2027 with Indian community leaders and NGOs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Education, economic opportunities, welfare and socioeconomic development were among the key issues discussed during a meeting between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Indian community leaders yesterday.
Human Resources Minister R. Ramanan said the second session of the meeting brought together leaders from nine chambers of commerce and 14 non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to discuss community perspectives, including inputs for Budget 2027.
He said the meeting represented the government’s ongoing effort to directly listen to and understand the views, aspirations and challenges faced by the Indian community.
“Every view, concern and suggestion was heard directly by the prime minister. This approach is essential to ensure policies and initiatives taking shape truly reflect ground realities and community needs,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Ramanan noted that the open, honest and constructive session was not the end of discussions, but part of a continuous engagement process.
“What was raised will be given appropriate attention and follow-up so that these discussions yield tangible benefits for the community,” he said.
He also expressed appreciation to the community leaders present for representing their respective organisations, reflecting the broader aspirations, needs and hopes of the Indian community as a whole.
He added that the government would continue to move forward with the people by listening, understanding and implementing the development agenda.
Also present at the meeting were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (MITRA) director-general N. Raveendran Nair. — Bernama

Title: PAS targets prime minister’s post, says no more ‘giving way’ to other parties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — PAS Youth delegates have urged the party to lead cooperation with other political parties while insisting that it has enough qualified candidates to lead the federal government.
PAS Kedah Youth chief Ilyas Ahmad said efforts to unite Muslims at the federal level should be led by PAS, which he said should no longer make way for other parties to put forward the prime ministerial candidate, according to a Malaysiakini report.
“We do not want to hear any more words such as ‘it’s okay, let someone else become prime minister’. We do not want to hear that anymore! This time, we want to ensure PAS becomes the main leader at the federal level,” he said.
He was speaking during the debate on the PAS Youth chief’s policy speech at the PAS muktamar here yesterday.
Ahead of the Johor state election on July 11, Barisan Nasional chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi told
Sin Chew Daily
that, if he became prime minister, he would focus on three areas — the economy, equitable education and national security.
Following BN’s strong showing in the election, the coalition subsequently forged an electoral cooperation with PAS through Perikatan Nasional (PN) based on the principle of Muslim unity.
However, there has been no official announcement so far on whether the two sides will cooperate in the upcoming Melaka state election.
Earlier yesterday, PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the party was ready for the 16th General Election (GE16), including if it were called earlier than scheduled.
His statement came after Zahid said Umno-BN wanted GE16 to be held earlier to allow the government to secure a fresh mandate from the people.
Meanwhile, PAS Terengganu Youth delegate Mukhlis Hasin echoed the Kedah representative’s view, saying PAS must lead efforts to forge unity rather than merely become a “follower”.
“Never be afraid to defend our identity simply because we want to preserve unity. We should not be afraid to defend the truth just because we want to maintain unity,” he said while debating the policy speech.
He said PAS Youth was not only responsible for uniting members at the grassroots level but also had to ensure the party leadership was prepared to make any efforts towards unity successful.
“Our biggest challenge in leading this unity is that sometimes the children (party members) want to unite, but their fathers (party leaders) have certain needs and reasons that prevent unity from being properly achieved,” he said.

Title: Teen TVET student found drowned after disappearing while crab hunting in Melaka
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 4 — A teenager, believed to have gone missing while looking for crabs in the coastal reclamation area near Pantai Klebang here, was found drowned late yesterday.
Melaka Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Fire and Rescue Operations Division, Senior Fire Superintendent II Mohd Shahrom Laji, said Muhammad Arif Daniel Nizamuddin, 16, a Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institution student, was found near the waters of Pulau Upeh at about 7:20 pm yesterday.
“The victim was found by fishermen near Pulau Upeh, about two nautical miles from the mainland, before the Search and Rescue team went to the location to retrieve the victim’s body.
“Identification of the victim’s body was carried out by family members at approximately 8:30 pm before it was handed over to the police for further action,” he said in a statement here yesterday.
Meanwhile, Melaka Tengah District Police Chief ACP Halim Abas, when contacted, confirmed the discovery of the victim’s body.
He added that the victim’s body was sent to the Melaka Hospital Forensic Department, and a post-mortem is expected to be conducted today.
The media previously reported that the victim, who was the youngest of two siblings, was feared drowned while catching crabs in the coastal reclamation area near Pantai Klebang here Wednesday.
During the incident at around 3:00 pm, Muhammad Arif Daniel was believed to have been swept away by strong waves or stepped into a deeper area before going missing.
Based on initial information, Muhammad Arif Daniel and a friend went to the area to catch crabs before he reportedly swam towards the open sea and was pulled under by waves before disappearing. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s chip ambitions: From assembly hub to semiconductor powerhouse
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Semiconductors are behind much of the technology people use every day, from smartphones and cars to bank cards, air-conditioners and the data centres powering artificial intelligence (AI).
Malaysia has been part of the global semiconductor industry for more than five decades and is now looking to move beyond its traditional strengths.
The country is particularly strong in the back end of the semiconductor supply chain — assembly, packaging and testing — but is seeking a bigger role in higher-value activities such as chip design, advanced packaging, semiconductor equipment and research and development.
So where does Malaysia stand today, and how is it trying to move up the value chain?
First, what exactly is a semiconductor?
A semiconductor is a material that can be used to control the flow of electricity.
Silicon is the most widely used semiconductor material.
Tiny electronic devices known as integrated circuits (ICs) — or simply “chips” — are built on pieces of semiconductor material.
These chips contain interconnected electronic components, including microscopic transistors that process electrical signals.
Different chips perform different functions.
Central processing units (CPUs) handle general computing in computers and servers, while graphics processing units (GPUs) perform large numbers of calculations simultaneously and are increasingly important for AI and data centres.
Memory chips store information in smartphones, computers and other devices, while microcontrollers control functions in products such as cars, washing machines and air-conditioners.
In other words, semiconductors are building blocks of the modern digital economy.
Smartphones use chips for processing, cameras and communications; cars use them for batteries, sensors and braking systems; while bank cards use them for secure transactions.
Where is Malaysia now?
Malaysia’s semiconductor industry began developing in the 1970s and has since grown into a large ecosystem involving multinational companies, local suppliers, engineers and technicians.
The country is particularly strong in the back end of the semiconductor supply chain — assembly, packaging and testing.
The Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) estimates Malaysia accounts for about 13 per cent of global back-end semiconductor assembly, testing and packaging and about 7 per cent of global semiconductor trade.
In 2024, exports of semiconductor devices, integrated circuits, transistors and valves amounted to RM387.98 billion, accounting for 64.5 per cent of Malaysia’s RM601.21 billion in E&E exports, according to the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade).
Investment data also shows continued interest in the broader semiconductor ecosystem.
According to Mida, Malaysia’s electronic components subsector recorded RM16.9 billion in approved investments in 2025, involving 59 projects expected to create 12,461 jobs.
Foreign investment accounted for RM14.6 billion, or 86.3 per cent, while domestic investment made up RM2.3 billion.
The momentum has continued into 2026, with Mida reporting RM218.5 billion in total approved investments in the first half of the year, including RM51.3 billion in manufacturing.
Of the manufacturing total, the E&E industry attracted RM16.6 billion, making it the largest category.
Why is the industry growing?
One major reason is the rapid expansion of AI, which requires enormous computing power and increasingly sophisticated chips.
Demand is also being driven by data centres, electric vehicles and advanced electronics.
Malaysia’s semiconductor exports rose from RM141.23 billion in January-April 2025 to RM212.12 billion in the same period of 2026, according to figures cited in a parliamentary reply by the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (MITI).
The increase reflects stronger global demand for semiconductors, including for AI-related applications, data centres and automotive and industrial sectors.
But attracting investment is only part of Malaysia’s semiconductor ambitions.
How is Malaysia trying to move up the value chain?
A simplified semiconductor supply chain runs from design to wafer fabrication, packaging, testing and eventually the finished product.
Malaysia has traditionally been strongest towards the back end, but the government now wants to develop greater capabilities in integrated-circuit design, advanced packaging, semiconductor manufacturing equipment and research and development.
Its goals are set out in the National Semiconductor Strategy (NSS), launched in 2024.
The NSS targets RM500 billion in combined domestic and foreign semiconductor investment by 2030, the development of Malaysian semiconductor companies capable of becoming global champions and the training of 60,000 high-skilled Malaysian engineers.
It also includes initiatives involving advanced packaging, IC design start-ups and a semiconductor park.
The strategy is therefore not simply about attracting more factories, but expanding Malaysia’s role across more parts of the semiconductor value chain.
From manufacturing to chip design
The shift towards higher-value activities can be seen in Malaysia’s partnership with British semiconductor technology company ARM Limited.
Under a four-year national partnership announced in 2025, the programme aims to train 10,000 semiconductor professionals and give selected Malaysian companies access to ARM technology and intellectual property.
On August 21, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said four companies had entered the design and IP-evaluation stage, while eight ARM technology access packages had been offered to five Malaysian companies.
The government is targeting locally manufactured chips developed through the ARM collaboration to enter production by 2030.
Akmal had said companies receiving the technology access could take about three years to develop their chip designs before production.
This illustrates the difference between attracting a manufacturing facility and developing semiconductor technology.
The government is also expanding into advanced packaging, building on Malaysia’s existing strength in assembly and testing while moving into more sophisticated technologies increasingly needed for AI and high-performance computing.
What does this mean for jobs?
The shift towards higher-value semiconductor activities could create greater demand for engineers, chip designers, researchers and skilled technicians, while giving Malaysian companies opportunities to develop and own more intellectual property.
Mida has also said its latest investment figures show a shift in semiconductor investment from back-end assembly towards front-end design and equipment, which it described as part of the operationalisation of the NSS.
For students considering a career in the industry, the pathway can begin with a strong Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) foundation at school, particularly in mathematics, physics, chemistry and computer science.
At university level, relevant courses include electrical and electronic engineering, electronic engineering, microelectronics, semiconductor and integrated-circuit design, computer engineering, mechatronics, materials science and physics.
Students can also enter the industry through polytechnics, community colleges and technical and vocational education and training (TVET) programmes, which can provide more hands-on training for roles such as semiconductor technicians, equipment technicians and manufacturing and testing specialists.
Depending on their interests, students could pursue chip design through backgrounds such as microelectronics or integrated-circuit design, while manufacturing, testing and equipment roles offer opportunities for engineering and TVET graduates.
These pathways could lead to careers ranging from technicians and engineers to chip designers, researchers and semiconductor equipment specialists.
What are the challenges?
Malaysia’s electronic components sub-sector also remains heavily reliant on foreign investment, which accounted for 86.3 per cent of approved investment in 2025.
The country also faces competition from other economies seeking the same investments and talent, while the semiconductor industry remains vulnerable to global economic cycles, trade restrictions and geopolitical tensions.
Training enough engineers — and retaining them in Malaysia — will also be crucial as the country tries to move from being a major semiconductor manufacturing base to a bigger player in chip technology and other higher-value activities.

Title: Serian records hazardous API 391, four other Sarawak areas at very unhealthy levels
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, September 3 — Air quality continued to deteriorate this afternoon, with Serian in Sarawak recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) of 391, putting it in the hazardous category, while four other areas in the state recorded very unhealthy readings.
Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said four areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy air quality, with Kuching registering an API reading of 285, Sri Aman 275, Samarahan 274 and Sarikei 206.
As of 5pm, 14 areas were classified as having unhealthy air quality, while 45 were at moderate levels and three were in the good category, she said.
Eight areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy air quality, with Sibu registering an API reading of 180, followed by Mukah (172), Bintulu (166), Samalaju (164), Kapit (157), ILP Miri (153), Limbang (151) and Miri (106).
Other areas recording unhealthy air quality included Politeknik Kota Kinabalu and Kota Kinabalu in Sabah, both at 156, Kimanis (155), Keningau (154), Labuan Federal Territory (157) and Johan Setia in Selangor (127).
“The country’s air quality has deteriorated today, with several areas, especially in Sarawak, Sabah and Labuan, recording API readings ranging from unhealthy to hazardous, influenced by haze moving in from different directions,” she said.
She said that according to an Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) report dated September 2, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) 20 satellite imagery detected 795 hotspots in Kalimantan, 144 in Sumatra and three in Malaysia, all in Sarawak.
She said the ASMC Regional Haze Map for the same date showed scattered hotspots across Kalimantan and Sumatra, while moderate to dense transboundary smoke haze covered northern Borneo and parts of the southwestern, western and central Philippines.
“Moderate to dense smoke was also observed originating from clusters of hotspots detected in several areas of Kalimantan and central and southern Sumatra.
“The Asean Secretariat activated Alert Level 3 for the southern Asean region from August 27, 2026 following an increase in hotspot activity and the wider spread of haze, based on ASMC monitoring, assessments and forecasts and in accordance with the Asean MAJER SOP (Asean Standard Operating Procedure for Monitoring Assessment and Joint Emergency Response),” she said.
She said the DOE would continue to monitor air quality through the National Haze Action Plan, with the relevant agencies taking action based on the situation and its developments. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia probes claim subsidised padi fertiliser smuggled into Thailand for bomb-making
Article:
PASIR PUTEH, September 3 — Malaysia and Thailand will use existing bilateral mechanisms to investigate allegations of bomb-making activities involving fertiliser elements from Malaysia, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the Malaysian and Thai police would conduct their respective investigations, with the matter to be managed through established channels, including government-to-government engagement, the Border Working Group and Police-to-Police (P-to-P) cooperation.
“The police will conduct an investigation, the authorities on their side will also conduct an investigation, and we will use the mechanisms that I mentioned,” he told a media conference after the handover ceremony for the completed Marine Police Base, Region Three project in Tok Bali here today.
He said that he would not want to respond directly to every allegation that emerged, stressing that border-related issues should instead be addressed through the mechanisms already established between the two countries.
According to him, the approach was important to prevent tensions from escalating or mutual suspicion from arising between the two sides, as Malaysia and Thailand had major responsibilities towards their respective peoples.
Saifuddin Nasution said the P-to-P cooperation enabled enforcement authorities from both countries to communicate and discuss security-related matters at any time, describing the mechanism as operating continuously.
Meanwhile, the Border Working Group serves as another platform for Malaysia and Thailand to discuss matters concerning the border, he said.
On the Region Three Marine Police Base, he said it is expected to begin operations in November with 111 officers and personnel to strengthen enforcement and maritime security along the East Coast.
The RM80.01 million project, implemented by PBLT Sdn Bhd, includes an administration building, boathouse, mechanical workshop, jetty, guardhouse, ammunition store and 82 quarters for personnel.
Saifuddin Nasution said the base would strengthen efforts to counter threats in East Coast waters, including drug and firearm smuggling, illegal immigrant and refugee landings, as well as incursions by fishermen.
“Most importantly, we are safeguarding the sovereignty of the country’s waters,” he said.
Also present were Bukit Aman Department of Internal Security and Public Order director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri and Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat. — Bernama

Title: Contractor: Muhyiddin’s Bersatu donation request wasn’t my imagination, I didn’t report it fearing abetment accusations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) president Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff today insisted that former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin told him in July 2020 that Bumiputera contractors who received Jana Wibawa projects could donate directly to the latter’s party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia.
Azman, who was testifying as the 27th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s power abuse trial, confirmed his previous testimony that he viewed Muhyiddin’s donation request as an offence.
Quizzed by Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, Azman confirmed that he had never lodged a police report against Muhyiddin over the donation request and disagreed that he had imagined the request.
Amer:
I’m telling you the reason why you didn’t make the complaint is because the so-called request is nothing more than a figment of your imagination.
Azman:
Disagree.
Later, when asked by lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin, Azman initially insisted that Muhyiddin had made the request, adding that he did not lodge a report as he “akur” or complied with Muhyiddin’s request.
But after a short break, Azman told the High Court judge that he wanted to correct his answer as he had remembered why he did not lodge a police report against Muhyiddin.
“I did not lodge a report because I don’t want to be accused of ‘bersubahat’ (abetting) Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin,” he said.
Among other things, Azman earlier today confirmed that Muhyiddin did not contact him in 2021 or 2022 to ask about any donations from contractors to Bersatu.
Amer then suggested that this meant the July 2020 discussion between Azman and Muhyiddin was merely a “creation” by the contractor so that he could “point the finger” at the former prime minister.
But Azman disagreed.
Earlier, Azman had said that Tan Sri Muhyiddin Charity Golf (TSMCG) committee member and Bersatu leader Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad was closer to Muhyiddin than he was.
But Azman disagreed with Amer’s suggestion that this meant Muhyiddin would not have asked him to tell other contractors to donate to Bersatu, and also disagreed that Muhyiddin would have asked someone close to him instead.
Former Prime Minister, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin is pictured at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Complex. — File picture by Firdaus Latif
Azman denies making deal with MACC in own corruption case, insists he’s innocent
Separately, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) had previously investigated Azman in 2023 over allegations that he had asked for and received bribes from contractors as a reward for helping them obtain Jana Wibawa projects.
Azman confirmed that the complaint that prompted MACC’s investigation mentioned his name but not Muhyiddin’s.
Azman confirmed to Amer that he had faced financial constraints when his accounts were frozen for nine months and agreed that the operations of his company KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and related company Addeen Engineering Sdn Bhd were disrupted during that period.
Azman agreed that he was under economic pressure in 2023 because of these events, but disagreed with Amer that this had caused him to “play ball” with MACC or that the commission had him “in their grip”.
Amer went on to suggest that Azman’s court testimony against Muhyiddin had been modified to fit MACC’s narrative and that he had tailored his testimony because he was under economic duress and pressure in 2023.
Azman disagreed.
Azman also disagreed with Amer’s suggestion that he had made a deal with MACC to testify against Muhyiddin and avoid being prosecuted, as his company KCJ Engineering would stand to lose its RM62 million Jana Wibawa contract if he were found guilty in court.
Lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin (pictured) questioned Azman Yusoff over why he did not lodge a police report against Muhyiddin. — File picture by Firdaus Latif
Later, when asked about the complaint that led to MACC’s 2023 investigation against him, Azman told the prosecution that the complaint was a “defamation” against him.
“That is a ‘fitnah’ (defamation) against me. I come to court to speak the truth, and I don’t care whether Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin wins or loses in this case. What is important, I am in court to speak the truth and I have already taken the oath,” he told Wan Shaharuddin.
Azman confirmed that he had not been remanded or charged in his own corruption case, but insisted that he had not committed any wrongdoing and claimed he was innocent.
Azman argued that bribery cases involved those with power, such as the prime minister, while saying that he himself did not have the power to award projects and that he had told contractors to donate to Bersatu if they obtained the projects.
Later, when explaining why he did not think the millions of ringgit received by his associated companies were bribes, Azman said he did not have the power to award projects, appoint contractors or receive donations, and also insisted that those in power would use their positions to ask for bribes.
Azman previously confirmed that his associated companies KCJ Engineering and Addeen Engineering received a total of RM9.35 million from several contractors, including RM1 million from Nepturis Sdn Bhd and RM600,000 from Mamfor Sdn Bhd.
Earlier, Azman insisted to Amer that the money he had received from those contractors was from “business deals” between companies and claimed that the payments were for technical advice he had provided on material costs for projects.
When clarifying why he had previously denied “selling” Muhyiddin’s name to obtain money from Bumiputera contractors Nepturis and Mamfor, Azman told the prosecution that he was “tidaklah sejahat” (not as evil) as to sell Muhyiddin’s name and added that he was indebted to the latter for his actions during the Covid-19 pandemic.
Azman concluded his testimony after confirming to the judge that he remains an Umno member.
Yesterday, MACC investigator Mazery Mohd Zaini said three Bumiputera contractors and their representatives had given RM25.3 million to Bersatu after obtaining Jana Wibawa projects, namely Azman and KCJ Engineering, which gave RM4.8 million; Nepturis, which gave RM1 million; and Mamfor, which gave RM19.5 million after its associated company Sutracom Sdn Bhd obtained a project.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, comprising four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia, from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd, and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin is scheduled to resume on September 14.
